hero.title: Google Gemini training: what it does, what each tier costs, and how to use it at work
hero.intro: Google Gemini ships four subscription tiers, three model generations, and deep integration across every Google app you already use — yet most professionals never move past the free chatbot. This Google Gemini training guide maps every tier, feature, and limitation so you pick the right plan and start producing results on day one.

sections.title: What is Google Gemini?
sections.body:
Google Gemini is [Google DeepMind's](https://deepmind.google/technologies/gemini/) multimodal AI model family. It powers both a consumer-facing app (web and mobile) and a set of developer APIs. Think of it as Google's answer to [ChatGPT](/ai-tools/chatgpt) and Claude — except it lives inside the Google ecosystem rather than standing alone.

The current generation, **Gemini 3**, launched in November 2025. The model hierarchy breaks into three tiers: **3 Pro** handles complex reasoning and creative tasks, **3 Flash** optimizes for speed at a fraction of the cost, and **2.5 Flash-Lite** handles high-volume processing at the lowest price point.

What sets Gemini apart from competitors is **multimodal input**. You can feed it text, images, video, audio, code, and PDFs — all in the same conversation. No plugins, no workarounds. Upload a recorded meeting, a spreadsheet, and a PDF contract, then ask Gemini to cross-reference all three.

The other differentiator is **native Google Workspace integration**. On paid tiers, Gemini appears as a side panel inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Meet. It drafts emails, summarizes documents, generates spreadsheet formulas, and creates presentation outlines — all without leaving the apps your team already uses.

Gemini is not a standalone product. It is an AI layer woven through Google's entire ecosystem. That's its greatest strength if you run a Google Workspace organization — and its biggest limitation if you don't.

sections.title: Gemini pricing plans and tiers (February 2026)
sections.body:
Google structures Gemini access into four consumer tiers. The jump between them is significant — not a gentle slope but a staircase, with each step unlocking meaningfully different capabilities.

| Feature | **Free** | **AI Plus** ($7.99/mo) | **AI Pro** ($19.99/mo) | **AI Ultra** ($249.99/mo) |
|---------|----------|------------------------|------------------------|---------------------------|
| AI credits | 50/day | 200/month | 1,000/month | 25,000/month |
| Context window | 32K tokens | 128K tokens | 1M tokens (~1,500 pages) | 1M tokens + Deep Think (192K) |
| Model access | 3 Flash (limited Pro) | Greater 3 Pro access | Highest 3 Pro access | All models + Deep Think |
| Image generation | Basic Nano Banana | Nano Banana Pro | Up to 1,000 images/day | Up to 1,000 Pro images/day |
| Deep Research | 5 reports/month | Included | 20 reports/day | Included |
| Workspace integration | No | Gmail, Docs (limited) | Full (Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, Chat) | Full + all advanced features |
| Storage | 15 GB | 200 GB | 2 TB | 30 TB |

*Pricing last verified: February 2026. USD figures corroborated from 9to5Google, TechCrunch, and Engadget — Google's official page renders in local currency.*

**Free ($0/month)** gives you 50 AI credits per day with Gemini 3 Flash and a 32K context window. You can try basic image generation and get five Deep Research reports per month. Enough to explore what Gemini can do — not enough for daily professional use.

**AI Plus ($7.99/month)** launched in the US on January 27, 2026 and reached 160+ countries. The jump to 200 monthly credits with a 128K context window makes it viable for regular use. You also get Nano Banana Pro image generation, Gemini inside Gmail and Docs, and family sharing for up to five people. For individuals who want more than the free tier but don't need full Workspace integration, this is the sweet spot.

**AI Pro ($19.99/month)** is where Gemini becomes a serious work tool. The context window jumps to 1 million tokens — roughly 1,500 pages of text. You get full [Workspace AI integration](https://workspace.google.com/solutions/ai/) across Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Meet, and Chat. Additional tools include the **Jules coding agent**, **NotebookLM Pro** (500 notebooks, 300 sources per notebook), the **Flow AI filmmaking suite**, and $10/month in Google Cloud credits. If you work inside Google Workspace daily, this tier pays for itself fast.

**AI Ultra ($249.99/month)** targets power users and researchers. It unlocks **Deep Think** (specialized reasoning that scored 84.6% on [ARC-AGI-2](https://arcprize.org/)), the **Gemini Agent** for multi-step task execution (200 requests/day), **Project Mariner** for browser automation, and 25,000 monthly AI credits. It also includes YouTube Premium and $100/month in Google Cloud credits. The price is steep, but the capabilities stand alone in Google's ecosystem.

**Which tier should you pick?**

- **Casual exploration:** Free tier.
- **Regular personal use:** AI Plus.
- **Daily professional work in Google Workspace:** AI Pro.
- **Research, engineering, or heavy automation:** AI Ultra.

For a deeper look at how these plans stack up against alternatives, see the [ChatGPT vs Gemini comparison](/ai-tools/compare/chatgpt-vs-gemini) and [Claude vs Gemini comparison](/ai-tools/compare/claude-vs-gemini).

sections.title: Core Google Gemini features every user should know
sections.body:
Gemini packs a long feature list. Here are the capabilities that matter most for daily productivity, with the tier that unlocks each one.

### Gemini Live

Voice conversations with Gemini, available on **all tiers** including free. You speak naturally, Gemini responds in audio. Useful for hands-free brainstorming, dictation, or working through ideas while walking. Think of it as a voice assistant that reasons — not one that follows commands.

### Image generation and editing (Nano Banana / Nano Banana Pro)

Gemini generates and edits images directly in the chat interface. The free tier includes basic **Nano Banana** generation. Starting at AI Plus, you get **Nano Banana Pro** with higher-quality output and advanced editing. The standout editing feature: circle, draw on, or annotate parts of an image and ask Gemini to modify those specific areas. No external image editor required.

### Deep Research

Deep Research runs multi-step research tasks automatically. You ask a complex question — "What are the environmental regulations for lithium battery recycling in the EU?" — and Gemini synthesizes information across multiple sources into a structured report. Free users get **5 reports per month**. AI Pro users get **20 per day**. For anyone who regularly compiles research, this feature alone can justify the subscription.

### Canvas

Canvas is Gemini's collaborative editing workspace. It opens a side-by-side panel where you and Gemini iterate on text, code, or other content together. Unlike a standard chat response you copy-paste, Canvas gives you a persistent working document you refine through conversation. Available on **all tiers**.

### Gems

**Gems** are custom AI personas you create for repeated tasks. Define a Gem with specific instructions — tone, context, constraints — and reuse it every time you need that workflow. A "Weekly Report Writer" Gem, for example, already knows your report format and data sources. You provide the raw inputs; the Gem produces consistent output. Available on **all tiers**.

### Google Workspace integration

This is Gemini's signature feature for organizations. On **AI Pro and above**, Gemini appears as a side panel inside Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Meet. Specific capabilities include:

- **Gmail:** Draft replies, summarize long threads, extract action items.
- **Docs:** Generate first drafts, rewrite sections, summarize documents.
- **Sheets:** Write formulas from natural language, analyze data patterns, generate charts.
- **Slides:** Create presentation outlines, generate individual slides from prompts.
- **Meet:** Real-time meeting notes, action item tracking, post-meeting summaries.

The integration requires no browser extensions and no copy-pasting between tabs. If your organization runs on Google Workspace, this is the feature that changes your daily workflow.

### NotebookLM

**NotebookLM** is a research and note-taking assistant that lets you upload sources (documents, websites, PDFs) and interact with them through AI-powered chat. A standout feature: **Audio Overviews** transform your uploaded sources into podcast-style audio discussions. The tool scales across tiers — basic access on free, expanded limits on Pro (500 notebooks, 300 sources per notebook), and full Ultra access with 200 Audio Overviews per day.

sections.title: Advanced features and agentic capabilities
sections.body:
Beyond everyday productivity, Gemini offers advanced tools that push into agentic AI territory — systems that take multi-step actions on your behalf rather than generating a single response.

### Deep Think

**Deep Think** is Gemini's specialized reasoning mode, designed for complex problems in science, research, and engineering. Deep Think scored **84.6% on ARC-AGI-2** (verified by the [ARC Prize Foundation](https://arcprize.org/)), achieved **gold-medal-level results** at the International Physics Olympiad 2025 and International Chemistry Olympiad 2025, and solved **multiple previously unsolved research problems** — including four open questions from Bloom's Erdos Conjectures database and disproving a decade-old mathematical conjecture from 2015.

Deep Think operates with a 192K token context window and caps at **10 prompts per day** on the AI Ultra tier. Lower tiers do not include it. If your work involves mathematical proofs, scientific modeling, or complex engineering problems, Deep Think offers the most capable reasoning mode in any consumer AI product today.

### Gemini Agent

**Gemini Agent** executes multi-step tasks autonomously. Give it a goal — "Research the top five competitors in this market and compile a comparison spreadsheet" — and it breaks the task into steps, executes each one, and delivers the result. You get **200 requests per day** with up to **3 simultaneous tasks**. Currently AI Ultra only, US only, English only.

### Project Mariner

**Project Mariner** automates browser actions. It navigates websites, fills forms, extracts data, and completes multi-step web workflows on your behalf. You can run up to **10 simultaneous tasks**. This moves Gemini from "answer my questions" to "do this task for me across the web." AI Ultra only, US only.

### Jules coding agent

**Jules** is an agentic coding assistant that goes beyond autocomplete. It understands codebases, writes multi-file changes, and executes code. AI Pro users get **5x limits** over base access; AI Ultra users get **20x limits**. For developers already working in the Google ecosystem, Jules integrates directly with [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/) and the Gemini API.

### Veo video generation

**Veo** generates cinematic-quality video from text prompts. AI Pro users access **Veo 3.1 Fast** with 3 videos per day. AI Ultra users get **Veo 3.1** with 5 videos per day, supporting 4K output and portrait video. The output quality positions Veo as a production tool, not a novelty.

### Flow and Whisk Animate

**Flow** is an AI filmmaking suite for creating and editing video content with AI assistance. **Whisk Animate** generates animated content. Both ship with AI Pro and AI Ultra. These creative tools round out Gemini's capability set for content creators and marketing teams.

### Computer Use (API)

Added in January 2026, **Computer Use** enables Gemini 3 models to interact with computer interfaces through the API — clicking buttons, navigating menus, and operating software. This is an API-only feature for developers building automated workflows.

sections.title: Gemini use cases by role — who benefits most?
sections.body:
Gemini's broad feature set means different roles extract different value. Here's a practical breakdown of who benefits most and which tier to choose.

**Knowledge workers (Gmail/Docs users):** If your day revolves around email, documents, and meetings, Gemini in Workspace eliminates hours of routine work. Draft email replies in seconds, summarize 30-page documents into key takeaways, and get automated meeting notes in Meet. Example: a project manager processes a 50-email thread into a one-page status update in under a minute. **Recommended tier: AI Pro.**

**Data analysts:** Gemini in Sheets writes formulas from plain-language descriptions, identifies patterns in datasets, and generates charts. For teams using BigQuery, the integration extends Gemini's analytical reach to large-scale data. Example: ask Gemini to "find the top 10 customers by lifetime value and create a bar chart," and it writes the formula chain for you. **Recommended tier: AI Pro.** For prompt ideas, see [best prompts for data analysis](/ai-resources/ai-prompts/ai-for-data-analysis).

**Developers:** Jules handles multi-file code changes, and Google AI Studio provides direct API access for building AI-powered applications. The Gemini API supports function calling, structured outputs, and code execution — all documented for production use. Example: a developer uses Jules to refactor a 200-line module, review the diff, and push the changes. **Recommended tier: AI Pro or AI Ultra** (depending on volume).

**Researchers:** Deep Research automates literature reviews and multi-source synthesis. Deep Think tackles problems that stump standard AI models — mathematical proofs, molecular modeling, complex data analysis. NotebookLM Pro organizes hundreds of sources into a searchable, interactive workspace. Example: a PhD candidate uploads 50 papers to NotebookLM and asks for a synthesis of methodological approaches across the corpus. **Recommended tier: AI Pro or AI Ultra.**

**Educators:** Gemini assists with lesson planning, generates personalized student feedback, and creates study materials. NotebookLM's Audio Overviews turn lecture notes into podcast-format review sessions students can listen to on the go. Example: a teacher uploads a unit plan and asks Gemini to generate five differentiated worksheets. **Recommended tier: AI Plus or AI Pro.** For more on AI in education, explore [AI training for educators](/ai-for-education/training/ai-for-teachers).

**Creatives:** Image generation with Nano Banana Pro, video creation with Veo, and the Flow filmmaking suite give creatives an AI-powered production pipeline inside a single platform. Example: a content marketer generates a blog header image, creates a 15-second promotional video, and drafts social copy — all within Gemini. **Recommended tier: AI Pro or AI Ultra.**

sections.title: What Gemini gets wrong — limitations you should know
sections.body:
No honest guide glosses over the rough edges. Here's where Gemini falls short.

**Hallucinations remain a real problem.** Gemini, like every large language model, generates plausible-sounding information that turns out to be wrong. Search grounding (connecting responses to Google Search results) reduces this but does not eliminate it. Verify critical facts before acting on them — especially numerical claims, legal citations, and medical information.

**Geographic restrictions lock out key features.** Gemini Agent, Project Mariner, and Personal Intelligence remain **US-only**. Deep Think requires **AI Ultra**. If you're outside the US or on a lower tier, several of Gemini's most advanced capabilities remain unavailable. Google has not announced expansion timelines.

**The credit system creates confusion.** Free users get 50 credits per day. AI Plus users get 200 per month. AI Pro gets 1,000 per month. Different features consume different amounts of credits, and the consumption rates lack transparency. Heavy users on the free tier hit limits within a few hours of active use. Google's documentation could do more to clarify how credits translate to usage.

**Workspace dependency limits value for non-Google users.** Gemini's strongest features — the side panel in Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Meet — require Google Workspace. If your organization runs on Microsoft 365, you lose the integration that justifies the premium tiers. For Microsoft-centric teams, [Microsoft Copilot](/ai-tools/copilot) provides a comparable experience within that ecosystem.

**Model versioning creates confusion.** Google maintains four version tracks for API models: Preview, Stable, Latest, and Experimental. Each behaves differently regarding stability and update schedules. The "Latest" alias hot-swaps to new releases with only two weeks' notice. For developers building production applications, this versioning complexity adds real operational risk.

**Knowledge cutoff applies.** Current Gemini models have a knowledge cutoff of **January 2025**. Search grounding helps bridge the gap for recent information, but it does not make the underlying model aware of events after its cutoff date. For time-sensitive topics, always verify currency.

sections.title: Gemini vs. the competition — where it fits
sections.body:
Gemini does not exist in isolation. Here's a quick positioning against three main alternatives — for detailed breakdowns, see the dedicated comparison pages.

**Gemini's edge:** Native Google Workspace integration gives it an unmatched advantage for organizations running on Google's stack. The free tier offers more than competitors (50 daily credits with image generation and Deep Research). Mid-tier pricing ($19.99/month for AI Pro) delivers strong value with a 1M token context window and full Workspace integration.

**Where ChatGPT wins:** A broader plugin ecosystem through the GPT Store, more extensive third-party integrations, and a larger user community producing shared workflows. If your needs extend beyond the Google ecosystem, ChatGPT's flexibility gives it an edge. See the full [ChatGPT vs Gemini comparison](/ai-tools/compare/chatgpt-vs-gemini).

**Where Claude wins:** Stronger performance on long-form writing tasks, more consistent instruction-following, and a stronger focus on safety and accuracy. For teams prioritizing careful, nuanced text output, Claude is often the better choice. See the full [Claude vs Gemini comparison](/ai-tools/compare/claude-vs-gemini).

**Where Copilot wins:** If your organization runs Microsoft 365, Copilot provides the same kind of deep integration that Gemini offers for Google Workspace. The choice often comes down to which productivity suite you already use. See the full [Copilot vs Gemini comparison](/ai-tools/compare/copilot-vs-gemini).

**Choose Gemini if:**

- Your team already uses Google Workspace and wants AI embedded in those tools.
- You need strong multimodal capabilities (text, image, video, audio) in a single platform.
- You want a generous free tier to evaluate before committing to a paid plan.

sections.title: Gemini tutorial: your first productive hour
sections.body:
Skip the theory. Here's how to go from zero to productive with Gemini in under an hour.

**Step 1: Access Gemini.** Go to [gemini.google.com](https://gemini.google.com) or download the Gemini app (iOS and Android). Sign in with your Google account. You're on the free tier by default — no credit card required.

**Step 2: Choose your plan.** Review the [pricing breakdown above](#gemini-pricing-plans-and-tiers-february-2026) and decide whether Free, AI Plus, AI Pro, or AI Ultra matches your needs. Upgrade from the Gemini app settings if needed.

**Step 3: Enable Gemini in Workspace (Pro/Ultra only).** If you're on AI Pro or Ultra and want Workspace integration, your Google Workspace admin enables it through **Admin Console > Apps > Google Workspace > Gemini**. Individual users on personal accounts get Workspace features automatically.

**Step 4: Run three starter tasks.** Try these to build immediate familiarity:

1. **Email draft in Gmail:** Open a long email thread, click the Gemini icon in the side panel, and ask it to "summarize this thread and draft a reply with next steps."
2. **Data question in Sheets:** Open a spreadsheet with data, activate Gemini, and ask "What trends do you see in this data?" or "Write a formula to calculate the month-over-month growth rate."
3. **Creative task in the Gemini app:** Open the Gemini app and ask it to generate an image, write a blog outline, or analyze a document you upload.

**Step 5: Create your first Gem.** Go to the Gems section in the Gemini app. Define a custom persona for a task you repeat regularly — a weekly report format, a code review checklist, a client email template. Give it specific instructions about tone, format, and context. Run it once to test, then refine the instructions based on the output.

You now have a working foundation. The next step is building real proficiency.
